transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

I guess I came in because... well, I've just been struggling a little bit lately, and I hope it's okay to talk about this here. I just can’t seem to stop feeling like everything that goes wrong around me is entirely my fault. I mean, I work in business operations, so I'm supposed to be the one keeping things running smoothly, you know? But lately, I just feel like I'm a really bad employee. 

And it's at home, too. I feel like I'm a terrible homeowner. It's embarrassing to even admit, but I just have this overwhelming sense that I deserve to lose everything I’ve worked so hard for. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm just overreacting or being dramatic. Does that make sense, though? Is that the kind of thing I should be bringing up?
Can you tell me more about these feelings of guilt and worthlessness? How often do they occur, and how intense are they for you?

Um, yeah, of course. I hope I'm not just repeating myself too much... but it's pretty much all the time right now. Like, every single day. 

It's just like I was saying, if anything at all goes wrong—even little things that I probably can't control—I just can't stop feeling like it's entirely my fault. I'll sit at my desk and just feel like I'm a fraud and a bad employee. And then I go home, and it's the exact same thing. I look around and just feel like I'm a bad homeowner, and that I honestly just deserve to lose everything I’ve worked for. 

As for how intense it is... well, it gets pretty heavy. It feels very real when it's happening. But I mean, I still log on for work every morning! I'm still getting my tasks done, so I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely falling apart or being a burden. I just can't seem to shake that constant guilty feeling, no matter how hard I try to rationalize it. 

I hope I'm explaining that right... is that what you were asking?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I still try to do things, I really do. I don't want to just sit around and mope, you know? 

But... I used to love planning brunches with my friends, and I'd paint in the spare room, or go hiking on the weekends. I'd even sign up for those professional networking events and actually look forward to them. Now, though... I don't know, it's just harder to get excited about it. I still go, of course! I don't want to let anyone down or seem anti-social. But when I'm there, it just feels like... like a task I'm just pretending to care about. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful for the things I have. I know I should be enjoying them. Is it normal to feel like you're just going through the motions like that?
Have you noticed yourself waking up earlier than usual and being unable to fall back asleep, especially in the early morning hours?

Oh, um... yes, actually. It's really perceptive of you to ask that. I didn't want to mention it earlier because I know everyone gets tired, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about being a little fatigued. 

But... well, most nights I just end up lying awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. And then, even when I do finally drift off, I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. After that, I just can't seem to get back to sleep before work. 

I still make sure I'm at my desk right on time, though! I promise I'm not letting it ruin my schedule or making excuses to log on late. I just kind of lie there quietly until my alarm goes off so I don't bother anyone. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions correctly.
Have you found yourself thinking about death or dying, or wishing you could just not wake up in the morning?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't want to die or anything like that! I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I would never want to do anything to hurt my family or, you know, cause a problem at work by just... not being here. 

I guess sometimes when I'm lying awake at four in the morning, I might have a fleeting thought that it would be nice to just... rest. Like, really rest without all the guilt and the exhaustion. But I always get up and start my day. I'm definitely not sitting around wishing I wouldn't wake up. I know I need to be responsible. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm in some kind of crisis or that I'm a danger to anyone. I'm really trying my best to handle things properly.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Um, well... I guess I have noticed a little bit of a change, maybe? I don't want it to sound like I'm slacking off at work, because I really do try to stay on top of all my tasks. I don't want anyone to think I'm not doing my job.

But... some mornings, it just feels like... like I'm moving in slow motion. Like I'm pushing through wet cement or something. Just doing simple things, like opening my spreadsheets or typing up an email response, or even just walking down the hall to a meeting... it all just takes so much more effort than it used to. I still get it all done, though! I make sure I finish everything I'm supposed to. I just... I might be a little slower than normal. 

I don't really feel restless or anything, just... heavy, I guess. Is that okay? I mean, is that a normal thing to experience when you're feeling this tired?
Have you ever had a period like this before, where you felt this kind of guilt, low mood, and exhaustion lasting more than a couple of weeks?

Um... well... I wouldn't exactly say I've had a different period like this, because... well, honestly, it hasn't really stopped. I'm sorry, I probably should have mentioned the timeline earlier. I just didn't want to sound like I was making a big deal out of things or, you know, complaining when everyone has stressful lives.

But the truth is, this low mood and... just kind of losing interest in everything... it's actually been with me for about two years and one month now. 

I've just been quietly pushing through it all this time. I really try not to let it show at the office, and I've kept up with all my performance metrics, I promise! I haven't let it drop the ball on any of my projects. I just... I thought if I tried hard enough, I could just fix it myself without bothering a doctor or being a burden to anyone. 

I hope you don't think poorly of me for waiting so long to finally say something. Am I... am I giving you the right information? I want to make sure I'm answering properly.
